name: Typewriter Loop
note: Types and deletes a rotating set of lines on a self-scheduling timeout chain with per-character jitter and longer pauses after spaces and punctuation; the caret stops blinking while keys are landing. The skip button switches to a 3-chars-per-frame fast delete and jumps to the next line. Reduced motion renders the first line statically.

name: Glyph Scramble Resolve
note: Mounts as a full block of glyph noise, then a rAF loop resolves it character by character — each cell gets a randomized start frame and settle frame, cycles hot glyphs while unresolved, and pops into place with an overshoot keyframe. A progress bar scaleX tracks how much of the word has locked; hover or the button advances to the next word. Reduced motion skips straight to the resolved word.

name: Word Mask Reveal
note: Each word sits in its own overflow-clipped box; a spring curve lifts them out on a 62ms stagger, holds the line, then flushes them upward in reverse order and loops. JS only toggles state classes — the stagger is a CSS transition-delay driven by a per-word --mo6wm-i index. Hovering the line lifts every word on a shorter stagger and postpones the exit until the pointer leaves.
html: Every word arrives on its own beat

name: Repulse Split Text
note: Letters are split into a bob layer and a fly layer so an idle sine bob and the hover scatter never fight over transform. On pointer move the JS measures each letter's untransformed box, computes an inverse-distance repulsion vector from the real cursor position and writes it to per-letter custom properties; CSS applies it with an overshoot spring and a centre-out delay. Keyboard focus fires a radial scatter and expands the shock ring.

name: Weight Wave
note: A travelling sine wave is evaluated per letter every frame and written to a single custom property, which CSS expands into stroke width, lift, scale, hue rotation, glow and an equaliser bar under each glyph — so one number drives a whole weight axis without a variable font. Moving the pointer plants a gaussian bump that eases toward the cursor and damps the travelling wave; leaving hands it back. Reduced motion paints one frozen wave.

name: Odometer Counter
note: Real odometer mechanics: each column holds three stacked 0-9 strips, and a change silently normalises the strip position then transitions a full extra revolution to the target digit, so every roll spins even when the digit barely moves. Columns fire on a 70ms right-to-left stagger under a decelerating curve with a motion-blur filter that lifts as they settle. Auto-ticks with a springing delta chip; tick and reset drive it by hand.

name: Velocity Skew Marquee
note: Two lanes drift at different base speeds and can be flung by dragging; pointer delta is smoothed into a velocity that keeps integrating after release under 0.94 friction. That velocity drives skewX and a horizontal stretch on both lanes at different gains, with the back lane lagging, and a live HUD reads the value out. Positions wrap modulo the measured sequence width (re-measured by ResizeObserver); arrow keys nudge velocity for keyboard users.

name: Gradient Sweep Headline
note: A 280%-wide gradient with a white hot band is clipped to the headline glyphs and swept across by animating background-position on an ease-in-out curve, while an accent rule grows from the left and wipes off the right on the same clock. Pointer X moves the glow behind the words and pointer Y tilts the gradient angle, both written on a rAF-throttled frame; hover doubles the tempo and runs a skewed screen-blend sheen over the top.
